speaker: Other
text: This is Supreme Court case number PRM06-006, re-amendments to miscellaneous rule 7.1 of the local rules of the Superior Court of Guam relief from disabilities. Appearing to present the amendments for promulgation is Judiciary of Guam staff attorney Daniel Menching. The panel consists of Chief Justice F. Philip Carbolito, Associate Justice Robert J. Torres, and Associate Justice Catherine A. Nerman.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, Mr. Menching. Before I recognize you, the order in which we are going to proceed is you will take address MR7.1 relief from disabilities, and then you will then go ahead and proceed and present on the amendments to MR1.1.5 regarding compensation to our private attorney panel. Thereafter, I will recognize the clerk of court who will then present on our court records retention policy. So at this time, Mr. Menching, you are recognized.

speaker: attomeydanielmen
text: Thank you, Mr. Chief Justice, Justice Torres, and Justice Nerman. May it please the court. The Supreme Court has before it amendments to miscellaneous rule 7.1 of the local rules of the Superior Court of Guam, which governs Guam's relief from disabilities program. Under both federal and local law, certain individuals are ineligible for firearm ownership due to prior adjudication of mental incompetence. Individuals who are subject to such adjudication are entered into the National Instant Criminal Background Check System. Miscellaneous rule 7.1, which was

speaker: danielmensching
text: enacted by the Guam Supreme Court in 2010, creates a relief from disabilities program in which an individual who has previously been adjudicated to have a mental defect may petition the court for relief from that determination for the purposes of the individual's ability to

speaker: attomeydanielmen
text: purchase a firearm. Having such a program is a requirement for Guam to be eligible for certain federal grants. The current version of rule 7.1 does not provide a mechanism for granted petitions to be entered into the relevant national databases which process firearm background checks. Such a mechanism is a requirement for relief programs to make a jurisdiction eligible for grants. The proposed amendments will bring rule 7.1 into compliance while also making minor technical adjustments and adding provisions which are common in programs from other jurisdictions, such as providing the Attorney General's Office with notice and an opportunity to object. The proposed amendments were sent to the Guam Bar Association for comment on February 25, 2022, with a comment period of two weeks. No comments were received. On behalf of the Administrative Office of the Courts, I now present these proposed amendments and ask that they be adopted and promulgated as presented to become effective immediately. Thank you.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, Mr. Menching. Does any of the justices have any questions for our staff attorney?

speaker: katnerineam
text: I don't have a question, but I'd also add that this is a recommendation from the CJAC committee in order to improve our access to criminal justice records and give persons with disability the opportunity to seek getting a gun permit again if they wish. And it's recommended by the CJAC committee. Thank you, Justice Merriman.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: So we will conclude the presentation on the amendments to MR 7.1. For the record, I ask the clerk just to call the topic for the next presentation.

speaker: Other
text: This is Supreme Court case number PRM 06-006, re-amendments to miscellaneous rule 1.1.5 of the local rules of the Superior Court of Guam indigent defense rule. Appearing to present the amendments for promulgation is Judiciary of Guam staff attorney Daniel Menching. The panel consists of Chief Justice F. Philip Carballito, Associate Justice Robert J. Torres, and Associate Justice Catherine A. Merriman.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you. Mr. Menching, you are recognized.

speaker: attomeydanielmen
text: Thank you, Your Honor. Mr. Chief Justice, Justice Torres, and Justice Merriman, may it please the court. The Supreme Court has before it amendments to miscellaneous rule 1.1.5 of the local rules of the Superior Court of Guam. The proposed amendments will increase both the hourly rates and the maximum compensation amounts for court-appointed attorneys. The amendments also create additional categories of compensation so that maximum payments will be more closely correlated with the seriousness of the offense.

speaker: danielmensching
text: The amendments further clarify some issues that have been brought

speaker: attomeydanielmen
text: to administration's attention by the Judiciary's Financial Management Division in their experience processing payments under the current rules, such as compensation in cases where multiple attorneys are appointed and how to compensate attorneys appointed in juvenile special proceedings cases, both of which are unaddressed in the current version of the rule. The amended rules also affect interpreter pay. By increasing the rates for registered, non-block hearings, and by clarifying that all interpreters paid on an hourly basis will be compensated to the nearest one-fourth fraction of the hour. The proposed amendments were sent to the Guam Bar Association for comment on February 9, 2022, and comments were accepted until February 17, 2022. Four comments were received from the Bar, three of which argued that the proposed rates were too low. The fourth comment stated that the Judiciary should further increase interpreter pay and hire full-time Chukes interpreters. Contrary to this suggestion, the Judiciary's current staffing pattern shows that the Judiciary currently employs three full-time Chukes interpreters, including David Welley, who leads the Judiciary's interpreter

speaker: danielmensching
text: program. In addition to the comments received from the Bar, the Administrator of the Court

speaker: attomeydanielmen
text: submitted a statement of support for the amendments, explaining that 10 other jurisdictions have been surveyed and that the new rules will put Guam equal to or ahead of almost all those jurisdictions. The Administrator of the Courts also explained the funding source for appointed attorney pay and the limitations on those funds, and while acknowledging the concerns of Bar members who provided comment, finds that increases above those contained in the proposed amendments would challenge the Judiciary's financial funds. While the many variables involved in compensation under these rules make it difficult to predict the exact financial impact of these amendments, the Judiciary's Financial Management Division has reviewed the amendments and projected that there will be roughly a 30% increase in expenditures if the amendments are put into effect. A new form which corresponds to the proposed rules has been prepared for attorneys to complete and submit to the Judiciary's Financial Division for processing a payment under the new rules. On behalf of the Administrative Office of the Courts, I now present these proposed amendments and ask that they be adopted and promulgated as presented to become effective May 1st. Thank you.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you, Mr. Menching. First of all, any questions to the staff attorney by any of the

speaker: katnerineam

speaker: Other
text: comments. Ms. Barrett, for the record. My other question is what happens if an attorney's voucher is discounted or changed and the amount they're paid, who did they go to? Is it the same process

text: Justice Merriman? Yeah, maybe it's not happening now, but there used to be occasions when for various reasons, the total amount requested was not paid and then the attorneys wanted to try and get that amount that wasn't paid restored. Is there a process if they have that situation?

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: And I take it you mean that not paid because it's in excess of the cap? No, under the cap. It might

speaker: Other

speaker: philipcarbullido

speaker: cour
text: Thank you, Chief Justice, and good morning, Justice Torres and Justice Merriman. In my experiences, we have not had anything of what you've described, those type of circumstances. The initial billings are first brought to CNM, who identifies the type of case, and then that determines caps. Then the attorneys file with FMD, and their FMD will review and audit what they're filing for, but I've never seen where FMD or even the administrator of the court's offices denied anything that didn't exceed the caps. So for the past two and a half years, nothing like that has occurred. As to the other question that you asked, I would like to add that under the new proposed changes to the miscellaneous rule, there is a statement there, a sentence there, that the Superior Court judge does have input into whether exceeding the cap is warranted. It doesn't require the judge to do the review, but they do have input under these rules changes. I would also point out that before, under the old rule, there was no gauge or factors that guided the administrator of the courts or the Superior Court judge as to what factors would warrant exceeding the cap. Under these proposed rules, there are factors that were researched and taken from other jurisdictions and added in, and this provides guidance to all parties. The counsel that is filing, also the judge if they're looking, and the administration's offices that are reviewing the billings that are coming in. And I did want to point that out, that we do have laid out factors that we follow when we look to a request from counsel to exceed the cap, and those provides us some guidance under these proposed changes. Thank you, Your Honors.

speaker: Other
text: Thank you. I'm satisfied there's a procedure for attorneys to resort to. Thank you.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you. Thank you, Justice Merriman. Justice Torres, any comments or questions for the staff?

speaker: roberttorres

speaker: philipcarbullido

speaker: Other
text: This is Supreme Court case number PRM06-006, three amendments to miscellaneous rule 6.1 of the local rules of the Superior Court of Guam on records retention. Appearing to present the rules for miscellaneous rule 6.1 for promulgation, is Superior Court Clerk of Court Danielle Rossetti. The panel consists of Chief Justice F. Philip Carbolito, Associate Justice Robert J. Torres, and Associate Justice Catherine A. Merriman.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Attorney Rossetti, you are recognized at this time.

speaker: glerk
text: Thank you, Your Honor. Mr. Chief Justice, Justice Torres, and Justice Merriman, may it please the court. On behalf of the Subcommittee on Rules Revisions, I am here this morning as a committee

speaker: daniellero
text: member to present proposed amendments to miscellaneous rule 6.1 of the local rules of

speaker: glerk
text: court on records retention. The records retention committee is a subset of the rules revisions committee chaired by Justice Torres. Members of the retention subcommittee also include judiciary staff attorneys, the clerk of courts for the Superior and Supreme Court, and other key judiciary staff. The rule on records retention originally existed in an appendix to Title VII GCA of the Guam Rules of Civil Procedure as Rule 93. In 2006, through promulgation order, the Guam Rules of Civil Procedure and Rule 93 were moved from Title VII to the local rules of court. Rule 93 is now miscellaneous rule 6.1. Over the last year, the committee met regularly to discuss amendments to the retention schedule and also worked to get VII GCA Section 7120 on the disposition of court records amended. The committee looked at retention schedules for various court jurisdictions as a model. The proposed retention schedule that is before the Supreme Court provides a schedule for both Superior Court and Supreme Court records. The schedule divides records that existed prior to 2011

speaker: daniellero
text: when we did not operate under the current electronic case management system,

speaker: glerk
text: also known as JustWare, and those records that were filed from 2011 to the present. Technology continues to advance and courts across the nation continue to improve the efficiency of cases through technology improvements. Electronic filing continues to expand and in many courts, e-filing is mandatory. Our courts have implemented e-filing for both the Supreme Court and Superior Court and hope to expand the Superior Court case types in the near future. The proposed schedule includes all case types filed in the Supreme Court and Superior Court, as well as other court records such as court audio recordings and jury records. The current retention schedule requires that all records be microfilmed before destroyed. The proposed schedule will allow for the retention of the records in a digital format before destruction and similar practices have been adopted in other court jurisdictions. Notice of the proposed rule was sent to the Guam Bar Association on January 24, 2022, and written comments were accepted through February 3. Notice of the virtual promulgation hearing was filed on April 4, 2022, and sent via listserv to the GBA members. The committee received two comments during the comment period. The first comment concerned the retention of land registration cases, specifically retaining the original certificates of title issued by the Department of Land Management and filed in a land registration case. The attorney recommended that land registration paper records be kept indefinitely and not destroyed. The second comment was on the retention of restitution cases. The concern was the time period for collection of restitution by a defendant and the proposed destruction of one year. The attorney recommended that the records be kept indefinitely or until restitution is completed. After speaking with the attorney about the comments, I clarified that court records are not destroyed if the case remains active. And therefore, that addressed the concern that the attorney brought to the committee for the proposed schedule that is before the Supreme Court. At this time, the retention subcommittee requests that the Supreme Court adopt and approve proposed rule 6.1 on records retention for Supreme Court and Superior Court records to be effective immediately upon promulgation and approval by the Supreme Court. And I will make myself available for any

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: questions that the panel may have. Thank you, your honors. Any questions or comments we have
